extracted.intended_audience: F99/K00 applicants, sponsor/co-sponsors, and F99/K00 review committee (NIH reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Materials and institutional/support documentation for an F99/K00 fellowship application, including mentor/sponsor statements, institutional environment, training plan, human subjects determinations, recruitment plans, and study timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring plan and mentor roles
rubrics_metrics.description: The sponsor/co-sponsor team will provide conceptual guidance, constructive feedback, and individualized training to the applicant; mentors will meet regularly (weekly mentoring meetings with Dr. Wu and Dr. Chi; biweekly consultations with Dr. Palinkas) and the primary sponsor (Dr. Chi) will coordinate communication among co-sponsors. Sponsors and co-sponsors will meet in-person once a year at major scientific meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors will guide intervention conceptualization, theoretical reasoning, intervention design, translation of analytical results to intervention mechanisms, purposeful sampling and mixed-methods planning, implementation/dissemination considerations, and manuscript preparation. The trainee is expected to request meetings proactively; sponsors will provide immersion training opportunities and oversee progress throughout the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods and methodological mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentorship specifically on mixed-methods research and implementation/dissemination science will be provided (Dr. Palinkas as an expert in purposeful sampling, mixed-methods implementation research, and implementation/dissemination science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor will help formulate purposeful sampling, data collection, and analysis plans, provide individualized methodological training, consult on intervention implementation processes, and assist in drafting intervention research proposals and manuscripts; biweekly consultation meetings are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and available research facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has access to institutional resources including the Suzanne Dworak Peck School of Social Work, Hamovitch Center for Science in the Human Services, USC Edward R. Roybal Institute on Aging, USC ADRC, and the Layton Aging and Alzheimer’s Disease Center (OHSU) with cores (outreach, recruitment and education, neuroimaging, data management and analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities and Other Resources and Description of Institutional Environment sections provide detailed resource descriptions. Mentors will direct the trainee to cores as research needs arise. Dedicated office space, a computer-equipped doctoral training lab, and opportunities to engage with university-wide seminars and centers are highlighted as training supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure and PhD coursework requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctoral students at USCSSW must complete a minimum of 45 course units beyond the master's degree (exclusive of the Doctoral Dissertation). First year: 8 courses (16 units) in social work policy, practice, and research; core substantive and research/statistics courses listed. Second year: advanced multivariate statistics and at least three courses per semester outside the school; at least eight of 12 units must be substantive courses rather than methods/statistics. Student-directed tutorials are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-year tutorials (2-unit) under a social work faculty mentor are intended to produce publishable-quality studies. Course lists include Theories of Human Behavior, Explanatory Theories, Introduction to Social Work Statistics, Multiple Regression, and Advanced Social Work Research Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying exam and advancement to candidacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the third year, doctoral students must pass a qualifying examination in their research area consisting of a written paper of publishable quality and an oral defense in order to be advanced to candidacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After passing the qualifying exam, students proceed to dissertation preparation: establishing an approved dissertation committee, submitting a dissertation proposal for approval, submitting the completed dissertation to the committee, and orally defending the dissertation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching requirement and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the third and fourth years, doctoral students must teach one course per year (can be co-teaching, teaching as an assistant, or solo teaching).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before teaching experiences begin, students must take a teaching course approved by the doctoral committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evaluation of trainee progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctoral program requires an End of Semester Report each semester (completed by the faculty mentor) and a yearly Progress Report Timeline to document milestones, deliverables (e.g., proposals, publications, presentations), and dissertation progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports are jointly signed by the student and mentor, submitted to the doctoral program director (and the graduate school for yearly reports), and are used as tools to guide and monitor each student's individual progress to ensure timely completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program outcomes and institutional commitment metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical program metrics include average time to degree (5.5 years), >95% of enrolled doctoral students completing doctoral studies, and 92% of recent graduates accepting academic research positions upon completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics and described program opportunities (research clusters, seminars, office space, training in grant writing) are presented to demonstrate institutional commitment to training and to make applicants competitive for academic positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of individuals across the lifespan (age justification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research focuses on older adults defined as age 65 or above; justification cites the Social Security Administration definition of 65 as standard retirement age and precedence in aging research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rationale emphasizes clinical and policy significance of focusing on older adults for ADRD research and explains the exclusion based on age for the aims of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of NHATS secondary data which is nationally representative with oversamples of oldest-old and non-Hispanic Black persons (baseline: 59.12% female, 20.52% non-Hispanic Black, 5.6% Hispanic). I-CONECT and CART do not exclude by race or gender and are still enrolling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus group participants will be purposefully sampled from I-CONECT to elicit diverse and rich information; purposeful sampling aims to recruit racially diverse participants and expects slightly more female participants given population composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and retention plan for qualitative focus groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus group participants will be recruited from I-CONECT participants via phone contact, with study purpose and participants' rights explained; availability will be recorded and participants will be asked to confirm attendance five days before the session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the focus group study is qualitative and not longitudinal, a retention plan is considered inapplicable; the plan emphasizes purposeful sampling and coordination with the I-CONECT research team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and clinical trials determination and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The application indicates whether proposed research involves human specimens/data, whether the project is exempt from federal regulations and the exemption number, and answers the Clinical Trial Questionnaire (prospectively assigned to interventions, designed to evaluate effect of intervention, health-related outcome).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide explanations for any use of human specimens/data not considered human subjects research, indicate ClinicalTrials.gov identifier if applicable, and select applicable exemption categories; examples and checkboxes are used to document determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population characteristics and eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions/focus: social isolation and cognitive functioning. Eligibility: participants of NHATS or participants of the I-CONECT clinical trial. Age limits: minimum age 65 years; no upper age limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollment status and anticipated enrollment dates should be specified; study timeline and recruitment materials (Recruitment_and_Retention_Plan.pdf) should accompany the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing datasets and research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research will utilize existing data from NHATS (large-scale longitudinal dataset), I-CONECT (Internet-based Conversational Engagement Clinical Trial), and the CART initiative; NHATS oversamples oldest-old and non-Hispanic Black older adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application notes that I-CONECT and CART are actively enrolling and that gender/racial breakdowns for those studies may not yet be available; using existing datasets is justified to achieve proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study timeline and specified research milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-year timeline enumerates activities including IRB submission, dissertation research (secondary NHATS analysis and manuscript preparation), systematic review development and manuscript, hands-on research with I-CONECT, CART investigations of longitudinal relationships, co-design of behavioral intervention (community partnerships, interview guide development, focus groups), and manuscript submissions across years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline chart indicates timing across F99/K00 years, anticipated participant enrollment date, and specifies deliverables (manuscripts, protocol development) aligned to training and research milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor/co-sponsor capacity and trainee supervision load
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of other trainees supervised by sponsors/co-sponsors (e.g., Dr. Dodge mentoring three postdocs; Dr. Palinkas supervising an F31 recipient; Dr. Kaye supervising postdocs) and the sponsors' record of NIH funding and mentoring experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is used to demonstrate that mentors have sufficient time and resources to support the trainee's dissertation and postdoctoral research and to show collaborative foundations (shared grants/projects) for co-mentoring arrangements.
